newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: High supply pushes tea prices down in Colombo.
newsitem.headline: High supply pushes tea prices down in Colombo.

text.p: Large availability and slightly lower quality pared tea prices at the Colombo auction on Wednesday, brokers said.

"Overall, it was a lower market today," said a trader at brokerage Forbes and Walker. "Prices dropped on the large quantities of tea which have been coming into the market and on their slightly inferior quality."
The anticipated average auction price for the 6.1 million kg on offer was 116 rupees ($1.98) per kg, against 119.84 rupees last week, Forbes said.

Most varieties of the island's distinct low growns, popular with Russian and Middle East buyers, were down. In the high growns, a few select best westerns added three to five rupees while some very bright Nuwara Eliyas moved higher, brokers said.
"Although the market was down, it is still selling at very good levels," said a broker for Eastern Brokers.
The next auction is on July 8-9, when 6.1 million kg will be on offer.
